outcome_detail: A civil trial covering the claims against Trooper Michael Miller was scheduled for March 3, 2025, in Kanawha County Circuit Court, per coverage from January 2024. Dedicated searches found no reporting on a trial result, settlement, or dismissal as of late July 2026.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges against Trooper Michael Miller had been reported as of the latest coverage found. The complaint states that hospital staff contacted a victim advocate who reported the incident to the FBI, and the allegations were part of the broader 2023 investigations into West Virginia State Police misconduct; the complaint also alleges the State Police and the Logan County Sheriff's Office failed to appropriately investigate Miller.
description: A woman sued West Virginia State Police Trooper Michael Miller, the West Virginia State Police, the West Virginia Department of Homeland Security, and American Legion Post No. 19 in Kanawha County Circuit Court in May 2023. According to the complaint, in December 2021 Miller was displaying his badge at the American Legion Post 19 club in Logan, and the woman recalled feeling as though she was about to pass out before waking the next day covered in blood, urine, and feces; the suit alleges Miller drugged, kidnapped, and raped her. The complaint states that the rape unit at CAMC Women and Children's Hospital confirmed she had been victimized and that the incident was reported to the FBI. The suit further alleges that the State Police and the Logan County Sheriff's Office knew of the allegations and failed to appropriately investigate. A trial date of March 3, 2025 was set; no outcome has been reported in available coverage.
notes: Companion record: rec-30b covers a second, separately filed lawsuit against the same trooper by a different woman (July 2021 incident). Both suits are part of the broader 2023 WVSP scandal that also produced the academy hidden-camera mass litigation (rec-29), but are separate cases.
